newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks jump to record high.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks jump to record high.

text.p: Australian shares jumped to an all-time high at the open on Monday, continuing their rally from Friday's record close to track Wall Street upwards.
At 10.25 a.m. (2325 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 14.3 points firmer at 2,409.9, eclipsing its previous intra-day high of 2,408.9 set on November 26.
Leading the market higher was Australia's largest company, BHP, which opened much firmer on moderate volume. BHP was trading at A$17.71 ($14.11), up 16 cents from Friday's close.
"Once the market got through the 2,400 level it was always going to surge ahead," said Derek Bond, a senior dealer at Brisbane brokerage Burrell and Co.
Bond said he expected the market to remain strong in the short term.
"It's a thin market and there are a lack of sellers out there," he said.
The big resource companies were finding the best support early although industrials were also higher with the bank and transport sectors well bid.
